To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the leaves of two chaparral shrub species, Ceanothas megacarpus (Ceanothaceae) and Ceanothas crassifolias (Ceanothasaceae), become more vertical in summer and this change is associated with a decrease in xylem pressure potential.

1) leaf orientation of two California chaparrl shrubs, C. megacarpa and C. crassi/olius, changes seasonally with the greatest changes occurring in the summer drought period; 2) leaf orientation changes are reversible, and, under favorable conditions, young leaves become horizontal in the spring, while older leaves become more horizontal in the summer drought; 3) the changes in leaf orientation are associated with changes in xylem pressure potential and leaf temperature;

1) predawn xylem pressures decreased during the summer drought, 2) leaf inclination became more vertical, 3) leaf azimuth was random, and 4) the increase in leaf inclinations during the summer reduced the amount of solar radiation intercepted by the leaves.

the relationship of leaf orientation to the drought response of two California chaparrals shrubs.
